bounds.name: determinism_bitwise
bounds.statement: Every determinism case must be bitwise identical across all repeats within a process, AND the per-case output/LSE digests must be identical across independent processes.

bounds.name: output_ulp_concentration
bounds.statement: At least 90% of characterized output elements must agree with the incumbent within 2 ULP.

bounds.name: output_max_abs_delta
bounds.statement: The largest output disagreement with the incumbent must be at most 4 bf16 steps at the scale of the tensor's own maximum. Expressed scale-free as max_abs_delta <= 4 * 2^-8 * reference_max_abs, evaluated per case and taken at its worst.

bounds.name: lse_max_ulp
bounds.statement: The fp32 log-sum-exp must agree with the incumbent within 8 ULP everywhere. LSE feeds the acceptance/rejection arithmetic, so it is held tighter than the bf16 output in relative terms.

bounds.name: lse_max_abs_delta
bounds.statement: Absolute LSE agreement, as a second check that does not depend on the ULP grid.

bounds.name: argmax_flips_vs_exact_no_worse_than_incumbent
bounds.statement: Against a float64 dense reference on the SAME probe cases, the candidate must disagree with the exact argmax no more often than the incumbent does. This is the bound that makes the arm-versus-arm flip rate interpretable: a disagreement between two approximations is not a defect unless the candidate is the worse approximation.

bounds.name: output_rms_vs_exact_ratio
bounds.statement: Candidate output RMS error against the float64 reference, divided by the incumbent's on the same case, at its worst. Catches a systematic bias that a ULP histogram would not: a kernel can be uniformly slightly wrong and still sit within 2 ULP everywhere.

bounds.name: lse_rms_vs_exact_ratio
bounds.statement: The same test on the log-sum-exp.

bounds.name: nonfinite_agreement
bounds.statement: No element may be finite in one arm and non-finite in the other, in output or LSE. A NaN or Inf that appears only under split-K is a defect, not a rounding difference, at any magnitude.

Author: claude-picktest <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 19 22:21:21 2026 +0000

    site 18: the credential's commit is recorded, not bound — one tier-scoped predicate
    
    _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b1_tier_b_credential required the credential's sealed
    identity.source_commit to equal the serve's commit. The credential is tracked,
    so seal at HEAD -> commit it -> HEAD moves -> every serve refuses, with no
    satisfiable ordering.
    
    Site 17's disease one layer down. Pass 101 moved source_commit out of the
    sidecar's TIERB_BINDING_FIELDS into TIERB_RECORDED_FIELDS; pass 108 scoped the
    launcher's selector gate to match; this container-side check was the THIRD
    statement of the same rule and got neither update. The cure for a rule stated
    in three places is not a third correction: there is now one predicate,
    _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b1_commit_binding(tier) -> "bound" | "recorded", and it
    REFUSES an unknown tier rather than defaulting, so a fourth route inherits the
    scope instead of picking one of the two rules by accident.
    
    RECORDED IS NOT IGNORED. Tier B now requires the sealed commit to be present,
    well-formed 40-hex, and -- the part a field comparison cannot give -- the value
    the rest of the credential was SEALED with, established by recomputing the
    canonical payload digest against credential_sha256. Change the commit and the
    digest changes, so a credential cannot carry a commit its own bounds and
    identity block never saw. It is carried into the serve record as
    credential_source_commit beside commit_binding: "recorded" -- provenance stated
    as provenance rather than smuggled in as a match. Byte-gated arms still
    compare: tier A's credential IS a byte identity earned at a commit.
    
    CENSUS, both roots, classified per pass-101 scope. Comparators: the launcher's
    ==HEAD x3 (already tier-scoped, pass 108), its 40-hex tier-B check x3, the
    gqa_pair serviceability probe (tier-A route), the sidecar's field lists (pass
    101), and the patcher's one -- which was the stale one. Every other
    source_commit touch in either root is a writer or a well-formedness check, not
    a comparator. One stale site, and the rest of the class is closed.
    scan_commit_binding_scope() now fails any B1 commit-vs-HEAD comparison that is
    not tier-scoped, mutation-proved by restoring the pre-108 launcher.
    
    REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded: untracked staging to make ==HEAD satisfiable.
    Making a retired rule satisfiable is not the same as applying the ruling, and
    once binding is recorded-not-bound a tracked credential no longer
    self-invalidates.
    
    Mutation proofs: tier-B serve on a credential sealed at an ancestor commit
    passes AND records that commit; a credential whose recorded commit was rewritten
    without re-sealing refuses as not self-consistent; malformed recorded commits
    refuse (with the env commit kept valid, so it is the credential's own value
    under test and not an earlier identity check); a byte-gated arm at a non-HEAD
    commit still refuses, driven through the shared predicate so it asserts the
    scoping rather than a second copy of it.
    
    This moves the patcher digest to 78206cc447e112686c068fb3a73916ac7f755e82ec58e5507504d4ca17788d6f
    -- re-seal #3, routine; the coupling test is red until it lands. Full sweep:
    zero new failures beyond that signal.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
